dedupe_keys.name: subsidised drought insurance for farmers in austria climate adapt case study

description: This case study describes Austria's subsidised public-private drought insurance for agriculture, which combines indemnity-based multi-peril insurance, such as the AGRAR Universal product, with weather index-based drought products linked to rainfall or the number of dry or hot days. Most products are offered by the Austrian Hail Insurance Association (Österreichische Hagelversicherung), a non-profit mutual owned by its policyholders, and public premium subsidies are financed by the Natural Disaster Fund (Katastrophenfonds), fed by taxes on income and on returns on capital and corporate profits; an amendment to the scheme was discussed in parliament in 2016 and 2017. It is published on Climate-ADAPT, the European Environment Agency's adaptation platform. Coverage is Austria, where insurance reaches almost 100% of horticulture, 70 to 75% of fruit and arable land and about 30% of grassland and livestock. The case study is available free online. Caveats: it is a descriptive summary drawing on cited studies, and the page does not report payouts or evaluation results. For simulation it gives a real risk transfer design and uptake rates for models of how insurance shifts drought losses from farms to public funds and insurers. It is related to the southwest Oklahoma drought insurance case study in this catalogue.
